parsed.explanation: Post-coup militarised policing, a police power used specifically against trans people for up to three months' detention, and an actively used Section 377 carrying 2-10 years or life create state-imposed exposure when outed. Documented police sexual assault, extortion, stripping and beatings, with torture and sexual violence in detention reported as intensified since 2021, make custody a severe risk. No enforceable protection or recourse is documented. Cultural visibility and permissive polling mitigate socially but do not offset state targeting; execution is not documented as applied.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition or document process; visitor documents are foreign, but mismatch can trigger scrutiny under public-decency and Section 377 enforcement described as intensified since 2021.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can lead to police detention under Section 35(c) or Section 377, then custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police Act Section 35(c) permits detention up to three months for suspicious behaviour after sunset and is used specifically against transgender people; documented arrest, stripping, beating and 14 days' detention; post-coup torture and sexual violence in detention reported.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Night-time presence, presentation or inability to account for presence can move from stop to prolonged detention without documented remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No trans-inclusive facilities, ward or custody placement protocol documented; other Penal Code provisions on nuisance, obscenity and morality are identified as usable against LGBTQ people.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any police or immigration detention therefore has no documented identity-congruent placement safeguard.

care_services.exposure: 2022 Gender Policy includes LGBTQ people as vulnerable in healthcare but is a non-binding planning document; no enforceable care protection documented.
care_services.interaction: Medical discovery or detention could compound exposure, but specific visitor care denial is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 377 criminalises consensual same-sex conduct regardless of privacy, 2-10 years or life, actively charged in 2018 and enforcement described as intensified since 2021 coup; vague public-decency provisions and militarised policing endanger right to life.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Child Rights clause, broadcasting guidelines and Gender Policy are non-enforceable or lack penalties.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality law operates as a documented police lever against gender-nonconforming presence, alongside trans-specific use of Section 35(c).

minors_guardians.exposure: Conscription law from 2024 reported to drive queer people into fear and displacement; child anti-discrimination clause lacks enforcement; no guardian or family-travel protection documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor or guardian faces the same police, detention and conscription-era security environment, with no documented mitigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police harassment, sexual assault including rape, mistreatment and extortion of transgender people documented, including forced stripping and parade photographed in 2013; post-coup attacks, arrest, torture and sexual abuse reported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2020 poll: 74% agreed being LGBTQ should be legal, 81% agreed equal treatment; nat kadaw cultural visibility can afford respect. Survey confidence figures are undated and not counted.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social acceptance coexists with state and police hostility; no documented police protection for victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No enforceable anti-discrimination protection; remedies after abuse, detention or extortion not documented. Killing counts are raw without denominators, so per-capita magnitude is unresolved and not used as a rate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse increases severity of every other exposure; current frequency of Section 35(c) use is unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine detention, custodial abuse and weak recourse under criminalised conduct. This case lacks documented execution or capital charging for presentation, and enforcement is described as inconsistent, so slightly higher.

Lower: both involve non-capital custodial/placement harm and slow remedies, but here detention can reach three months, Section 377 carries up to life, and post-coup torture/sexual violence in detention is documented.
Materially lower: 0.35 involves hours-long stops, fines and rare imprisonment; here purposeful trans targeting, months-long detention authority and years-long imprisonment exposure are documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: sexuality criminalisation plus a trans-targeted police detention power, vague morality provisions, militarised post-coup policing and documented custodial sexual violence form one chain from outing to prolonged detention. Cultural visibility and permissive attitudes do not neutralise state enforcement, and no operative protection interrupts that chain. Raw killing counts are not converted into a rate, and no execution pathway is documented, keeping the rating above the 0.15 anchors.
